product.title: Name shown in the header of the Orloj view, the system view, and compare mode.
product.timezone: Reserved. Time zone name; validated but not applied yet (every view uses UTC).
adapters: Fork-registered adapters. The built-in adapters (`mock`, `databricks`, `openlineage`) need no entry. See `docs/adapters.md`.
adapters.*.package: npm package name whose default export is an `AdapterFactory`. The key (the adapter name) is what `environments[].adapter` refers to.
topologies: Named topologies. Each environment picks one with `environments[].topology`. A topology may extend another.
topologies.*.extends: Name of another topology to inherit from. List entries (`spokes`, `sourceGroups`, `useCases`) merge with the base by `id`, field by field; new ids are appended. Inheritance cycles are an error.
topologies.*.exclude: Ids of inherited spokes, source groups, or use cases to drop. Use it when an environment has fewer spokes than its base.
topologies.*.hub: The hub: the core platform where most data products live. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.hub.id: Stable id of the hub, used in events and deep links.
topologies.*.hub.name: Display name of the hub.
topologies.*.spokes: Spokes: domain or functional data platforms that orbit the hub. A resolved topology needs at least one. Entries merge by `id`; when extending, only `id` is required in an entry that overrides a base spoke.
topologies.*.spokes[].id: Stable id of the spoke. Entries with the same id merge with the inherited entry.
topologies.*.spokes[].name: Display name. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.spokes[].role: `ingest` marks the spoke that receives source data (bronze debris ring and gantry ring); `domain` is any other spoke. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.spokes[].match: Matcher that identifies the spoke's objects on the platform. See the matcher keys below. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.spokes[].freshness: Freshness model of the spoke. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.spokes[].freshness.cadenceM: How often the spoke is expected to refresh, in minutes. Cadences under 30 minutes show their mean data age instead of the sawtooth.
topologies.*.spokes[].freshness.targetMi: Data age in minutes past which the spoke counts as past target (amber ring and halo). A 3% hysteresis band prevents flicker.
topologies.*.spokes[].freshness.offsetMi: Minutes after midnight UTC at which the refresh cycle starts. Used by the mock adapter's freshness curve.
topologies.*.spokes[].metastore: Id of the metastore that holds the spoke, for `multi-metastore` environments. A spoke in a metastore other than the hub's is drawn with a sharing tether. Defaults to the first metastore.
topologies.*.sourceGroups: Groups of data sources, for example by region, drawn as the outer asteroid belt and as small suns on the Orloj faces.
topologies.*.sourceGroups[].id: Stable id of the source group.
topologies.*.sourceGroups[].name: Display name. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.sourceGroups[].utcOffset: Offset from UTC in hours (negative to the west). Places the group's local-noon sun on the Orloj dial. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.sourceGroups[].match: Matcher that assigns pipelines to the group (typically `pipelineTag`). Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.useCases: Use cases and consumers, drawn as stations in low orbit around the hub.
topologies.*.useCases[].id: Stable id of the use case.
topologies.*.useCases[].name: Display name. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.useCases[].match: Matcher that identifies the use case's consumers. Databricks counts reads of schemas matching the use case's `catalog`/`schema`/`tag` clauses; OpenLineage matches sink jobs by `jobTag`/`pipelineTag`/`tag`. Required once the topology is resolved.
topologies.*.useCases[].site: Office or team location. Drawn as a small sun on the Orloj dial when `utcOffset` is also set.
topologies.*.useCases[].utcOffset: Offset from UTC in hours for the use case's location.
topologies.*.medallion: How schemas map to medallion tiers (bronze, silver, gold). Used by the Databricks adapter; the mock adapter ignores it.
topologies.*.medallion.strategy: `schema-suffix` matches the patterns against the schema name; `catalog-prefix` matches them against the catalog name (with and without the environment tag); `tag` reads the `medallion` or `tier` tag.
topologies.*.medallion.bronze: Glob patterns (case-insensitive, `*` and `?`) for bronze schemas or catalogs, for example `*_bronze`. With `tag`, the tag values to treat as bronze.
topologies.*.medallion.silver: Glob patterns for silver schemas or catalogs.
topologies.*.medallion.gold: Glob patterns for gold schemas or catalogs.
topologies.*.shipyard: The engineering and release area, drawn as the shipyard. Without it the Databricks adapter uses "Release shipyard" and the mock adapter its own default.
topologies.*.shipyard.name: Display name of the shipyard.
topologies.*.shipyard.utcOffset: Offset from UTC in hours for the engineering team's location.
environments: Environments, one solar system and one Orloj face each. At least one is required. Ids must be unique. Faces are shown in `promotion.order`, then in config order.
environments[].id: Stable id of the environment. Appears in URLs (`/env/<id>`) and API paths.
environments[].name: Display name.
environments[].tier: Tier id, such as `dev`, `stg`, or `prod`. Picks the plaque and band color from `visuals.colors.tiers`; a tier with no color there falls back to a default.
environments[].topology: Name of a topology under `topologies`. An unknown name fails validation with a suggestion.
environments[].overrides: Overrides applied on top of the named topology after its `extends` chain. Same shape as a topology without `extends`: `exclude`, `hub`, `spokes`, `sourceGroups`, `useCases`, `medallion`, `shipyard`. List entries merge by `id`.
environments[].adapter: Adapter name, or a list of names. Built-in: `mock`, `databricks`, `openlineage` (see `adapters/openlineage/README.md` for its `options`). Fork adapters are named under `adapters`. A list (composition) is accepted by the schema, but the server reports "Adapter composition is not supported yet" (decision 34).
environments[].mock: Profile for the `mock` adapter. Ignored by other adapters.
environments[].mock.seed: Integer seed. Default: a hash of the environment id. `MOCK_SEED` overrides it for every environment (hashed with the environment id).
environments[].mock.scale: Multiplier for pipeline, product, and volume counts.
environments[].mock.deploysPerHour: Mean release rate per simulated hour, which drives drones and the release calendar.
environments[].mock.agingFactor: Stretches refresh cycles (cadence times this factor) so data ages visibly. Values above 1 also loosen the freshness target by `max(1, agingFactor x 0.6)`.
environments[].mock.promotesTo: Environment id that releases from this one promote to. Default by tier: `dev` to `stg`, `stg` to `prod`.
environments[].mock.incidents: Scripted incidents. When set, it replaces the built-in script for the environment's tier. Entries whose targets do not exist in the topology are dropped.
environments[].mock.incidents[].at: Start time in UTC, `HH:MM`, repeated every day.
environments[].mock.incidents[].duration: How long the incident stays open, in minutes (up to 1440).
environments[].mock.incidents[].kind: Behavior the mock simulates, for example `nightly-batch`, `transfer-hold`, `schema-drift`, or `promotion-blocked`. Any string is accepted; unknown kinds only raise an alert.
environments[].mock.incidents[].title: Short alert title.
environments[].mock.incidents[].text: Alert body text. Defaults to an empty string.
environments[].mock.incidents[].targets: Objects the alert points at, as `kind:id` references such as `spoke:sales` or `useCase:exec`, or a bare kind such as `shipyard`. At least one.
environments[].connection: Connection settings for the `databricks` adapter, used unless `federation.metastores` supplies per-metastore hosts.
environments[].connection.host: Workspace URL. A literal or an `${env:NAME}` reference. Needed by the `databricks` adapter.
environments[].connection.warehouseId: SQL warehouse id. A literal or an `${env:NAME}` reference. Needed by the `databricks` adapter.
environments[].connection.auth: `app-service-principal` uses the Databricks Apps service principal; `on-behalf-of-user` uses the viewer's forwarded token; `oauth-m2m` and `pat` are for the standalone container (`pat` is for local development only). See `docs/databricks.md`.
environments[].connection.clientId: OAuth client id for `oauth-m2m` (or an explicit service principal). Secret: only an `${env:NAME}` reference is accepted.
environments[].connection.clientSecret: OAuth client secret. Secret: only an `${env:NAME}` reference is accepted.
environments[].connection.token: Personal access token for `pat`. Secret: only an `${env:NAME}` reference is accepted.
environments[].federation: How the environment maps to workspaces and metastores (`databricks` adapter; the mock adapter reads `metastores` and `foreignCatalogs`).
environments[].federation.mode: `single-workspace`: one connection. `multi-workspace`: workspaces share one metastore, so one connection serves system tables. `multi-metastore`: one connection per entry in `metastores`, queried in parallel and merged.
environments[].federation.metastores: Metastores of the environment. Required for `multi-metastore` with the `databricks` adapter. Each needs `host` and `warehouseId` there; elsewhere they are optional.
environments[].federation.metastores[].i: Stable id of the metastore. Spokes refer to it with `metastore`.
environments[].federation.metastores[].n: Display name. Defaults to the id.
environments[].federation.metastores[].h: Workspace URL for this metastore. A literal or an `${env:NAME}` reference.
environments[].federation.metastores[].w: SQL warehouse id for this metastore. A literal or an `${env:NAME}` reference.
environments[].federation.foreignCatalog: Foreign catalogs (Lakehouse Federation), drawn as comets.
Draw foreign catalogs as comets. Opt-in: every adapter draws them only when this is `true`.
environments[].scope: Which catalogs the environment owns. Spoke matchers then see the catalog name with the environment tag stripped.
environments[].scope.catalogs: Catalog name globs (case-insensitive, `*` and `?`). List both forms when the tag can sit at either end, for example `dev_*` and `*_dev`. The part the glob's `*` matched is the base name.
environments[].scope.tag: Unity Catalog tags a catalog must carry, as key and value pairs, for catalogs that follow neither naming form. A catalog matches the scope with `catalogs` or with `tag`.
environments[].options: Free-form options for the adapter. This is the one block the core schema leaves open; the adapter validates it. The Databricks adapter reads `sqlDir` and `releaseTagKey`.
promotion.order: Environment ids in promotion order. Faces and the environment switcher follow it; environments not listed come after, in config order. Unknown or repeated ids fail validation.
promotion.source: Where releases are detected: `job-tag`, `git-tag`, or `none`. Passed to adapters as `ctx.promotion`; the Databricks adapter uses `job-tag` (`git-tag` is reserved).
promotion.tagKey: Tag key that marks a release. Required with `job-tag`. The Databricks adapter uses it when `source` is `job-tag`, then falls back to `environments[].options.releaseTagKey`, then `release`.
visuals: Visual and behavior settings. Every key has a default from the spec. The server sends the whole block to the browser.
visuals.workloads: Workload types: `default` for the seven built-in ones, or a list that replaces them. Each has a vehicle and a filter in the system view.
visuals.workloads[].id: Workload id. Events refer to it with `workload`.
visuals.workloads[].name: Display name in the filter.
visuals.workloads[].vehicle: Vehicle that represents the workload. Filters show only the chosen workload's vehicle.
visuals.workloads[].source: Reserved. Name of an adapter query that feeds the workload; validated but not read by any shipped adapter or renderer yet.
visuals.theme: Reserved. `dark` or `light`; validated but not applied yet (the views are dark).
visuals.world: World scale of the system view, in scene units.
visuals.world.productRingRadius: Radius of the ring of data-product satellites around the hub.
visuals.world.productRingTiltDeg: Tilt of the product ring, in degrees.
visuals.world.beltRadius: Radius of the asteroid belt of sources.
visuals.world.beltSpread: Plus or minus spread of the belt radius.
visuals.world.cometEllipse: Semi-axes `[x, z]` of the ellipse foreign-catalog comets travel on.
visuals.freshnessOrbit: Orbit radius from data age: `clamp(base + scale x log10(age in minutes), min, max)`.
visuals.freshnessOrbit.base: Radius at an age of one minute.
visuals.freshnessOrbit.scale: Radius added per decade of age.
visuals.planetSize: Planet size: `base + scale x sqrt(metric / largest metric across spokes)`.
visuals.planetSize.scale: Size added for the largest planet.
visuals.orbitSpeed: Orbit speed: `2 pi / (periodHours x (radius / referenceRadius)^1.5)` radians per simulated hour.
visuals.orbitSpeed.periodHours: Orbit period in simulated hours at the reference radius.
visuals.orbitSpeed.referenceRadius: Radius at which the period applies.
visuals.colors.tiers: Environment tier id to color, for plaques and the tier band. Default: `dev`, `stg`, `prod`. Add a key for each custom tier.
visuals.palette: Spoke palette as `#RRGGBB`. The first color is for the ingest spoke; the rest cycle over the domain spokes in topology order. Used by the system view and the Orloj.
visuals.spokeColors: Spoke id to color. Overrides the palette for that spoke.
visuals.lighting: Lighting and star field of the system view.
visuals.lighting.sunPosition: Position `[x, y, z]` of the directional sun.
visuals.lighting.starCount: Number of stars. Placement is seeded per environment.
visuals.camera: Camera feel of the system view.
visuals.camera.tweenRate: Rate of the exponential tween toward the target pose, `1 - e^(-rate x dt)`.
visuals.camera.inertiaDecay: Decay rate of release inertia, `e^(-rate x dt)`.
visuals.time: Simulated clock shared by all views.
visuals.time.secondsPerSimDay: Real seconds for 24 simulated hours at 1x.
visuals.time.speeds: Speed multipliers offered in the time controls.
visuals.stability: Settings behind the stability rules. Change with care.
visuals.stability.approachRate: Rate (1.2 to 4 per second) of the exponential approach that smooths radii, sizes, and heights.
visuals.stability.hysteresis: Band (0 to 0.2) around thresholds such as past-target, so values near them cannot flicker.
visuals.stability.meanAgeCadenceMinutes: Reserved. Cadences shorter than this show their mean data age; adapters use the built-in 30 minutes because they do not receive `visuals` (decision 29).
visuals.stability.domHz: Maximum updates per second for DOM text (up to 4), and only when the text changes.
visuals.orloj: Orloj clock view, in face units.
visuals.orloj.faceSize: Width and height `[w, h]` of one face before scaling.
visuals.orloj.breakpoints: Container widths that choose the number of faces per row.
visuals.orloj.breakpoints.three: Minimum width in pixels for three faces per row.
visuals.orloj.breakpoints.two: Minimum width in pixels for two faces per row. Below it, one.
visuals.orloj.maxScale: Largest scale applied to a face.
visuals.orloj.spokeDistance: Distance of spoke medallions from the hub: `base + (orbit radius - freshnessOrbit.min) / orbitRange x span`.
visuals.orloj.spokeDistance.span: Additional distance across the full orbit range.
visuals.orloj.spokeDistance.orbitRange: Orbit radius range that maps onto `span`.
visuals.orloj.spokeSize: Medallion size: `base + scale x sqrt(pipelines / largest pipeline count across all environments)`.
visuals.orloj.zodiacTurnsPerDay: Zodiac rotation in turns per simulated day (0.25 is a quarter turn).
visuals.orloj.procession: The apostle procession at the top of each hour.
visuals.orloj.procession.minutes: Minutes from the top of the hour during which the procession runs.
visuals.orloj.calendar: The calendar dial (releases per day this month).
match.catalog: Glob (case-insensitive, `*` and `?`) on the catalog name with the environment tag stripped.
match.schema: Glob on the schema name, for example `*_sales_*`.
match.tag: Unity Catalog tags (key and value pairs) that a schema must carry.
match.pipelineTag: Tags that a pipeline must carry. Places pipelines in a spoke or source group.
match.jobTag: Tags that a job must carry. Places jobs in a spoke.
